strengths: Soundness: The controlled dataset separates positional generalization, unseen configurations, and generalization to categories seen only in single-object training. This provides a useful setting for studying relational transfer without visual recognition confounds.

Mechanistic evidence: The attention decomposition is complemented by inference-time interventions. Figure 5 and Appendix G show that removing the EP contribution substantially reduces relational retrieval while preserving object-pair identification, supporting a specific role in spatial discrimination.

Originality and significance: The contribution is a useful empirical account of how positional attention gradients emerge under contrastive training. Experiments with inverse captions, RoPE, and head pruning broaden the investigation beyond one visualization.

Presentation and limitations: The main experimental progression is understandable, and the manuscript explicitly acknowledges unresolved questions about natural images, deeper networks, and interacting heads. The synthetic data present no apparent material privacy or human-subject concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—label diversity is not isolated: The two-object training set contains n2 × Npair × (Npair − 1) examples. Increasing label diversity therefore also increases dataset size quadratically, changes the single-object/two-object balance, and, under conventional epoch accounting, increases optimizer updates. Varying n2 also changes sample count rather than independently controlling layout diversity. Figures 3–4 establish correlations but do not justify the central claim that label diversity is the primary driver. Matched-data and matched-update comparisons are needed.

Soundness—the theoretical necessity claim exceeds the derivation: Appendix I derives |Π| > |T| for a head to preserve its directional preference after swapping two objects. It does not establish that this property is necessary for successful retrieval by the complete multi-head model. The argument omits value representations and output aggregation; Appendix H itself demonstrates a contribution from positional values. Moreover, held-out pair categories receive single-object training, so their token-dependent terms cannot simply be treated as unconstrained. The result should be framed as a condition for the proposed attention mechanism.

Statistical support: The principal accuracy curves report neither variation across training/data seeds nor uncertainty estimates. Unseen-pair evaluation uses only five held-out categories and five images per ordered pair. Several curves are nonmonotonic, and detailed mechanistic conclusions rely on selected trained models. Replication across seeds and held-out category splits is important before treating these patterns as reliable properties of training.

Reproducibility: Although many architecture and training hyperparameters are supplied, the manuscript does not specify the optimizer, contrastive temperature/logit-scale treatment, random seeds, or code availability. Batch handling of repeated captions and the two equivalent captions per image is also unclear; ordinary diagonal CLIP targets can treat semantically equivalent examples as negatives.

Significance and scope: The strongest causal analysis concerns a single-layer model without LayerNorm or MLPs. Appendix L provides only a qualitative first-layer decomposition for a deeper model, and the two-layer text mechanism needed for inverse captions remains unexplained. The simplified setting is legitimate, but the evidence supports a narrower architectural finding than the concluding promise of practical guidance for VLM spatial reasoning.

Presentation: Figure 5(d)'s caption gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific attention, contradicting the main-text definition. Several ablation captions repeat PP where PE appears intended. These errors directly affect interpretation of the central mechanistic experiments.

strengths: Originality and significance: The controlled 1D testbed provides a useful setting for studying how contrastive training acquires spatial discrimination. Holding categories out of two-object training while including them in single-object training meaningfully tests compositional transfer.

Soundness: The attention-logit decomposition and inference-time ablations provide evidence that positional contributions support left–right discrimination in the analyzed models. Appendix G strengthens this finding by showing that object-pair recognition survives when relational accuracy deteriorates.

Experimental breadth: The appendices investigate weight decay, positional values, RoPE, head pruning, and a two-layer vision encoder. These extensions add substance beyond illustrative attention maps.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The main experimental progression is understandable, and the discussion appropriately acknowledges the restricted synthetic setting and unresolved multilayer mechanisms. The synthetic data present no apparent material privacy or human-subject concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—confounded central data claim: Increasing Npair increases the number of two-object training examples as n2 × Npair × (Npair − 1). With fixed epochs and batch size, this also increases optimization steps and changes the single-object/two-object training balance. Consequently, Figures 3–4 do not isolate label diversity from data volume and compute. Varying n2 alone does not resolve this confound. Matched-data and matched-update experiments are needed to support the claim that label diversity is the primary driver.

Soundness—the theoretical necessity claim exceeds the derivation: Appendix I.1 establishes |Π| > |T| as a condition for one head to preserve directional preference under an object swap. It does not establish that this head-level property is necessary for successful retrieval using multiple heads and positional values. The subsequent assertion that unseen-pair token contributions are unpredictable is also unsupported: these categories were trained as single objects. The stronger |Π| ≫ |T| requirement and claimed necessity for generalization therefore do not follow.

Mechanistic scope: The ablations establish dependence on components in particular trained models, but do not isolate monotonicity itself from other information carried by the removed terms. Moreover, in the one-layer CLS row, the query token is fixed, so the EP contribution is a learned absolute-position preference rather than an object-dependent relational computation. This can implement a useful solution, but stronger claims require interventions on the gradient and analysis of how attention, values, and output projections jointly implement the decision. Appendix L supplies a two-layer visualization rather than equivalent causal validation.

Reproducibility and uncertainty: The manuscript specifies many architectural and training parameters, but does not report independent seed counts, uncertainty across training runs, optimizer identity, contrastive temperature handling, or a code availability statement. The multiple n2 curves are experimental conditions, not replications. Since the argument depends on learning transitions and selected heads, robustness across initializations and dataset draws is important. Handling repeated captions and equivalent positive captions within the standard contrastive loss also needs clarification.

Presentation and technical consistency: Figure 5(d)'s caption gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific behavior, contradicting Section 5. The main text describes positional-value ablation as reducing accuracy to 0.5, whereas Appendix H and Figure 17 attribute that outcome to jointly removing positional attention and value contributions. Appendix I.3 also incorrectly bounds ρaρb/(ρa² + ρb²) in (0, 1/2] without a same-sign assumption; it can be negative. These issues affect interpretation of the mechanism.

Overall significance: The specialized testbed and empirical mechanism have merit; natural-image experiments are not inherently required. However, the present evidence does not securely establish either the central diversity claim or the stronger necessity claim. Together with missing robustness and reproducibility details, these weaknesses prevent acceptance in its current form.

strengths: Significance: The controllable 1D testbed addresses a useful question: when contrastive training learns object order rather than merely object co-occurrence. Separating positional, configuration, and unseen-pair generalization makes the experimental setting informative.

Soundness: The attention-logit decomposition and inference-time ablations provide evidence that positional attention contributions support relational discrimination in the reduced model. Appendix G strengthens this finding by showing that object-pair recognition survives interventions that impair order recognition.

Originality: The contribution lies in mechanistic understanding rather than a new architecture. Complementary directional heads, the RoPE experiments, and the head-pruning studies offer interesting observations about how these small models encode order.

Presentation and limitations: The main narrative is coherent, and the dataset construction and most architectural parameters are described explicitly. The discussion appropriately acknowledges the unresolved transfer to natural images and deeper models. The synthetic setting raises no apparent material research-ethics concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—label diversity is confounded with training scale. The two-object training set contains n2 × Npair × (Npair − 1) examples. Increasing label diversity therefore also increases dataset size, the number of distinct pair constraints, and, with fixed epochs and batch size, optimization steps. Figures 3–4 do not isolate these effects. Varying n2 separately does not establish that label diversity is the primary driver; matched-data and matched-update comparisons are needed for this central claim.

Soundness—the theoretical necessity claim exceeds the derivation. Appendix I.1 correctly derives |Π| > |T| for a particular head to preserve its directional preference after swapping two objects. It does not establish that such a preference is necessary for successful retrieval by the complete multi-head model, whose values and combined outputs can also carry positional information. Furthermore, held-out pair labels were trained individually, so their token-dependent terms are not simply unconstrained. The analysis supports a possible mechanism, not a general necessity theorem for unseen-pair generalization.

Reproducibility and robustness: The manuscript does not report independent training seeds, uncertainty across runs, or how representative models were selected for mechanistic analysis. This matters because the generalization curves are irregular and several conclusions rely on individual heads in selected models. Optimizer details, contrastive temperature, and the treatment of duplicate or semantically equivalent positive captions within batches are also unspecified; no code availability statement is provided.

Soundness and presentation: Section 5 says ablating the positional value contribution reduces accuracy to 0.5, but Figure 17 shows that ablating VP alone largely preserves performance; chance-level performance follows the combined removal of positional attention and value terms. Figure 5(d)'s caption also gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific behavior. These inconsistencies affect interpretation of the central mechanism and should be corrected.

Significance and scope: The strongest causal evidence concerns a single-layer model without LayerNorm or MLPs. Appendix L supplies qualitative first-layer patterns for a deeper model, but does not establish that the same mechanism explains the original architecture's generalization. This restricted setting can still support a useful contribution, but broader claims of practical guidance require stronger evidence. Overall, the useful observations do not yet overcome the experimental confounds and overstatement of the theoretical result.

strengths: Soundness: The synthetic testbed cleanly distinguishes single-object positional generalization, unseen configurations of familiar pairs, and combinations of categories seen only individually. This makes the demonstrated compositional transfer more informative than ordinary retrieval accuracy.

Mechanistic evidence: The attention-logit decomposition is exact for the simplified architecture, and the interventions go beyond attention visualization. Removing EP substantially reduces relational accuracy while largely preserving object-set recognition (Fig. 5, Appendix H). Appendix M corroborates this with both left/right caption forms.

Originality and significance: Identifying learned directional attention gradients provides a useful, focused mechanistic observation. Extensions to RoPE, 2D layouts, three-object scenes, and head pruning broaden the investigation beyond a single illustrative model.

Presentation and limitations: The main experimental progression is understandable, and the manuscript explicitly acknowledges unresolved questions about natural images, nonlinear components, and interactions across layers. The synthetic data and stated impact assessment raise no material ethical concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—diversity is confounded with data and optimization scale. The training set contains approximately 5Ntot + n2 Npair(Npair−1) examples. Increasing label diversity therefore increases both the number of training examples and optimizer updates under the fixed 10,000-epoch schedule, while changing pair coverage and the balance of single- versus two-object examples. Moreover, n2 measures configurations per pair, not total layout diversity across the dataset. Figures 3–4 establish an association, but do not isolate label diversity as the primary driver. Matched-data and matched-update experiments are needed for this central claim.

Soundness—the theory establishes a narrower result than claimed. Appendix J derives |Π|>|T| as a condition for one head to maintain its directional preference under an object swap. It does not establish that this preference is necessary for successful multi-head retrieval, which also depends on values, output projections, and the text encoder. The assertion that held-out token contributions are unpredictable also overlooks their single-object training. The empirical ablations support reliance on positional terms in the examined models, rather than a general necessity theorem for relational generalization.

Mechanistic interpretation remains incomplete. With a fixed CLS query in the one-layer model, the EP contribution is an input-independent positional scoring function. This supports directional pooling, but does not by itself distinguish explicit positional comparison from position-dependent role encoding. Three-object training and ablations in Appendix N are useful extensions, yet do not exclude richer role-based representations. Likewise, deleting EP removes the entire contribution, so a matched intervention that flattens or reverses its gradient would more specifically test the claimed mechanism.

Reproducibility and robustness: No independent training-seed counts or uncertainty estimates are reported for the main accuracy sweeps and ablations. The unseen-pair evaluation uses only five held-out categories and five configurations per ordered pair, making variation across training runs and dataset draws particularly relevant. Appendix B links upstream repositories rather than the modified implementation; details such as contrastive temperature, duplicate-positive handling, and the embedding-alignment fitting procedure are insufficiently specified.

Presentation and evidential precision: Fig. 5(d)'s caption gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific cases, contradicting the main definition. Section 5 describes value-position ablation as reducing accuracy to 0.5, whereas Appendix I attributes that result to jointly removing positional attention and value terms. The nonlinear and autoregressive extensions show compatible attention patterns, but lack corresponding causal validation. These distinctions should be corrected so the conclusions consistently match the demonstrated evidence.

strengths: Soundness: The controlled dataset distinguishes single-object positional generalization, seen-pair configuration generalization, and composition of labels previously observed only individually. This provides a useful setting for studying spatial discrimination without perceptual confounds.

Mechanistic evidence: The attention-logit decomposition is exact for the attention-only models, and interventions go beyond visualization. Table 2 reports an unseen-pair accuracy decrease from 82% to 55% after EP ablation, while Appendix H checks that object-pair recognition is largely preserved. This supports a specific contribution of positional attention to ordering discrimination.

Originality and significance: Identifying complementary directional heads and tracing their behavior to positional logit components provides useful mechanistic understanding. Extensions to bidirectional captions, 2D grids, three-object scenes, and RoPE substantially broaden the investigation within synthetic settings.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The main experimental progression is understandable, and the paper candidly discusses incomplete transfer to three-object scenes and uncertainty about deeper and natural-image models. The synthetic data present no apparent material ethical concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—diversity is confounded with data and optimization scale. The training set contains approximately 5*Ntot + n2*Npair*(Npair−1) examples. Increasing label diversity therefore also increases training-set size, the proportion of relational examples, and optimizer updates under the fixed 10,000-epoch schedule. Figures 3–4 do not isolate these factors. The central conclusion that label diversity is the primary driver requires comparisons matched for sample count and training updates.

Soundness—the theoretical necessity claim exceeds the derivation. Appendix J establishes |Π| > |T| as a condition for one head to preserve its directional preference when two objects swap positions. It does not establish that this preference is necessary for successful retrieval by the complete multi-head model, including its value and output pathways. Moreover, held-out pair labels were trained individually, so their projected embeddings are not simply unconstrained. The derivation characterizes a possible mechanism rather than proving necessity for generalization.

Soundness—ablations support dependence on positional components more strongly than the claimed positional-comparison algorithm. Removing an entire EP term removes all of its positional structure, not specifically its monotonic gradient. Gradient reversal, magnitude-matched perturbations, or restoration interventions would better isolate the proposed mechanism. Likewise, the three-object results do not exclude richer absolute-position or role-based representations, despite the stronger interpretation in Section 9.

Reproducibility and statistical reliability: The manuscript does not report independent training-seed counts or uncertainty across runs for its central accuracy curves and ablations. Several extensions emphasize representative or best-performing models without a selection protocol. Appendix B links upstream repositories rather than the modified implementation; contrastive temperature and handling of equivalent captions as negatives in the main experiments are also insufficiently specified. These omissions matter for conclusions about emergence and architectural requirements.

Significance and scope: The strongest causal evidence concerns shallow attention-only models operating on symbolic object IDs and fixed relation tokens. Appendix R provides observational evidence of similar gradients in a nonlinear model, but not corresponding causal validation. This does not invalidate the toy contribution, but limits its demonstrated explanatory reach for standard CLIP-style encoders.

Presentation and technical precision: Figure 5(d)'s caption gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific behavior. Appendix J incorrectly states that the right-hand side of Eq. 31 is always positive without assuming matching signs for the positional scores. It also describes alignment between key-space principal components and right singular vectors of WK, although under the stated dimensions those inhabit different spaces. These errors need correction, particularly because they occur in the mechanism's quantitative justification.

strengths: Soundness: The controlled dataset separates single-object positional generalization, seen-pair configuration generalization, and generalization to pairs of categories seen only individually during training. This makes the demonstrated compositional transfer meaningful and interpretable.

Mechanistic evidence: The attention-logit decomposition is complemented by interventions. Removing EP substantially reduces relational accuracy while largely preserving object-set recognition (Fig. 5 and Appendix H), providing stronger evidence than attention visualizations alone.

Significance: The appendices substantially extend the core experiment through RoPE, 2D layouts, bidirectional descriptions, three-object scenes, and autoregressive training. In particular, the three-object intervention reduces complete-relation retrieval from 82% to 28% when EP is removed (Table 4).

Originality: The contribution is a useful empirical account of how directional attention specialization emerges during contrastive training, rather than a new attention decomposition. Connecting this specialization to transfer across object identities is a worthwhile mechanistic research direction.

Presentation and ethics: The main experimental progression is understandable, and the discussion appropriately acknowledges the distance from natural-image VLMs and the unresolved effects of depth and nonlinear components. The synthetic setting presents no evident material ethical concerns.
weaknesses: Soundness—diversity is confounded with data and compute: Increasing Npair also increases the number of two-object training examples as n2 × Npair × (Npair − 1). With fixed epochs and batch size, this increases optimization steps as well. Moreover, n2 controls configurations per pair, rather than independently controlling global spatial coverage. Figures 3–4 therefore do not establish that label diversity itself is the primary driver. Matched-example and matched-update controls are needed for this central claim.

Soundness—the necessity claim exceeds the analysis: Appendix J derives |Π| > |T| for a head to preserve its directional preference under an object swap. It does not establish that successful model-level relational discrimination requires such a head, particularly with multiple heads and position-dependent values. The assertion that unseen-pair token contributions are unpredictable is also unsupported: those categories receive single-object training. The theory should be framed as a characterization of the observed mechanism, rather than a general necessity result.

Mechanistic interpretation: Zeroing entire positional logit terms establishes their causal contribution in the trained models, but does not isolate monotonicity itself or establish an explicit positional-comparison algorithm. Gradient reversal, position permutation, or controlled replacement interventions would sharpen that conclusion. Likewise, the three-object results do not by themselves exclude richer role-conditioned representations, as the discussion suggests.

Reproducibility and uncertainty: No repeated-seed results or uncertainty estimates are reported for the generalization curves and mechanistic interventions. The unseen-pair evaluation uses only five held-out categories and five configurations per ordered pair. Appendix B links upstream repositories rather than the modified implementation, and details such as seed handling, contrastive temperature, and duplicate/equivalent-caption treatment in the main experiments remain unclear. These omissions make the robustness of the reported trends difficult to assess.

Presentation and scope: Several statements need correction or qualification. Figure 5(d)'s caption gives the same inequality for relational and label-specific behavior. Section 5 describes removing the positional value contribution as reducing accuracy to 0.5, whereas Appendix I and Fig. 17 attribute that result to jointly removing positional attention and value contributions. The extensions to nonlinear and autoregressive models primarily show gradient visualizations, so causal conclusions established in the reduced encoder should not automatically carry over.
